history.dynasty: Vijayanagara Empire (major patrons from the 14th century); collector Sir Thomas Munro developed the Raja Gopuram 1801-1807; now administered by Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD)
history.period: Legendary installation by Kripacharya (Dwapara yuga per Sthalapurana); documented patronage from the 14th century; inscriptions on temple walls dated 1396-1629
history.summary: Famous 'Toli Gadapa' (first threshold) to Tirumala, at Devuni Kadapa (Patha Kadapa / old Kadapa), about 3 km from Kadapa city; pilgrims traditionally have darshan here before Tirumala. Sthalapurana: during vanavasa, Rama installed a Hanuman idol here hoping Hanuman would help find Sita; in Dwapara yuga, Kripacharya (Dronacharya's brother-in-law), unable to reach Tirumala in old age, installed the Venkateswara idol in front of Hanuman - hence the puranic name 'Kripavathi Kshetram', and the temple faces west in Vijayanagara style. From the 14th century Vijayanagara rulers Harihara, Bukkaraya, Saluva Narasimharayulu and Krishnadevaraya developed it; inscriptions record donations from 1396 (crown by Sri Aranam Sarvappa) through 1629, including by Sadasiva Deva Maharaya (1480) and Maha Mandaleswara Timmaya Deva Maharaj (1484). Tallapaka Annamacharya worshipped here, praising the Lord as 'Kadapa Rayudu'. The place-name 'Kadapa' itself derives from 'Devuni Gadapa' (threshold of the Lord). name: Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple, Devuni Kadapa
town_description: Devuni Kadapa (also called Patha Kadapa, 'old Kadapa') is the historic core of Kadapa city in YSR Kadapa district, Andhra Pradesh, in the Rayalaseema region, about 3 km from the present city centre. It is the traditional starting point for Tirumala pilgrimages, famous for this west-facing Vijayanagara-style temple and as an example of local Hindu-Muslim harmony.
